evidence: Shell/Active_Shellference.sh select_action(): the for loop iterates over environment_ref with variable 'action' but calls calculate_efe(beliefs_ref preferences_ref transition_probs_ref) without using 'action' — all EFE computations are identical, meaning the selection logic always assigns selected_action to the last environment element (since min_efe is updated every iteration with the same value)

Rust/run.sh lines 38-44 and 43-46: nested if [ $? -eq 0 ] checks after 'cargo build --release' and 'cargo run --release' — with 'set -e' active at top of script, non-zero exit codes would already abort the script before these checks run, making the if/else branches unreachable dead code
Rust/run.sh lines 38 and 43: the 'if [ $? -eq 0 ]' pattern is redundant with 'set -e' — the else branches (echo '❌ ... failed'; exit 1) are dead code paths that can never execute
Cpp/run.sh lines 40-62: same dead code pattern — 'if [ $? -eq 0 ]' check after make under set -e; the failure branch is unreachable

run_all.sh line 245: 'TOTAL_IMPLEMENTATIONS=$(echo "${LANGUAGES[@]}" | wc -w)' — this counts whitespace-separated words in the array when converted to a string, but array elements contain no spaces, so wc -w gives the element count; however 'echo "${LANGUAGES[@]}"' concatenates all elements with spaces, so the word count actually equals the number of elements — the logic works but is indirect and misleading

run_all.sh lines 248-252: 'if [ $SUCCESS_COUNT -eq $TOTAL_IMPLEMENTATIONS ]' — TOTAL_IMPLEMENTATIONS counts array elements using word count, SUCCESS_COUNT counts successes; if SPECIFIC_LANG is set, only 1 language runs but TOTAL_IMPLEMENTATIONS is still 34, so this condition can never be true in single-language mode

Shell/Active_Shellference.sh calculate_vfe(): function body is 'vfe=$(calculate_kl_divergence ...) ; echo "$vfe"' — this is an identity wrapper that adds no computation, creating unnecessary indirection with no behavioral distinction from calling calculate_kl_divergence directly

status_dashboard.sh show_recent_activity() line 184-185: uses '-printf' flag with find but macOS does not support -printf by default — always-false condition on macOS silently produces no output without error

strengths: Most shell scripts use 'set -e' consistently, providing predictable early-exit behavior
Command existence checks ('command -v ... &> /dev/null') are a consistent pattern across all run.sh files
Python code in Student_Teacher.py uses clear, direct conditional structures without redundant branches
logic_clarity.issue_character: The dominant pattern is dead code from 'if [ $? -eq 0 ]' checks placed after commands under 'set -e', and one significant logical defect where select_action() iterates over actions without ever varying its computation per action.
logic_clarity.score_rationale: The score is significantly reduced by the select_action() logic defect (it never actually differentiates actions — the entire action-selection purpose of the function is broken) and the pervasive dead code pattern in Rust/run.sh and Cpp/run.sh where post-command $? checks under set -e can never reach their failure branches. The TOTAL_IMPLEMENTATIONS counting bug in single-language mode is a further clarity failure. These are real logic defects, not style issues.

issues.summary: Active_Shellference.sh select_action() computes identical EFE for every action because the action variable is never passed to calculate_efe()
evidence: Lines 167-175: 'for action in "${environment_ref[@]}"; do ... efe=$(calculate_efe beliefs_ref preferences_ref transition_probs_ref) ...'
The variable 'action' from the loop is not passed to calculate_efe()

Since min_efe starts at 1000000 and all EFE values are identical, selected_action is set on the first iteration and then unchanged only if subsequent EFEs are never lower — or may update spuriously based on floating point equality
issues.suggestion: Pass the action index to calculate_efe() so that transition probabilities for that specific action are used; update calculate_efe() to accept an action index parameter and apply action-specific transition probabilities

issues.summary: Rust/run.sh checks $? after cargo build and cargo run under set -e, making the failure branches unreachable dead code
evidence: Line 6: 'set -e' makes any failing command abort the script immediately
Line 36: 'cargo build --release'
Line 38: 'if [ $? -eq 0 ]; then' — if cargo build fails, set -e has already aborted; this check can only be true
Lines 71-78 (else branch): 'echo "❌ Rust build failed."' is dead code that can never execute
issues.suggestion: Remove the 'if [ $? -eq 0 ]' wrapper and run the success-path code directly, relying on set -e for failure handling; or remove set -e and keep the explicit checks consistently

issues.summary: Cpp/run.sh has same dead code pattern as Rust/run.sh: $? checks after make and ./ActiveInferenceDemo under set -e
evidence: Line 6: 'set -e'
Line 38: 'make'
Line 40: 'if [ $? -eq 0 ]; then' — failure branch at lines 60-62 is dead code under set -e
issues.suggestion: Same fix as rust_run: remove the $? wrappers and rely on set -e, or remove set -e and use explicit checks consistently

issues.summary: run_all.sh compares SUCCESS_COUNT to TOTAL_IMPLEMENTATIONS after running a specific language, but TOTAL_IMPLEMENTATIONS is always 34 regardless of how many were actually run
evidence: Line 245: 'TOTAL_IMPLEMENTATIONS=$(echo "${LANGUAGES[@]}" | wc -w)' — always counts all 34 languages
Lines 184-196: when SPECIFIC_LANG is set, only 1 language runs incrementing SUCCESS_COUNT to at most 1
Lines 248-252: 'if [ $SUCCESS_COUNT -eq $TOTAL_IMPLEMENTATIONS ]' — condition 1 -eq 34 is always false in single-language mode; 'All implementations completed' message never displays
issues.suggestion: Track TOTAL_RUN separately from TOTAL_IMPLEMENTATIONS, incrementing it only for languages actually attempted, and compare SUCCESS_COUNT against TOTAL_RUN

issues.summary: Active_Shellference.sh calculate_vfe() is an identity wrapper over calculate_kl_divergence() with no additional computation
evidence: Lines 69-76: calculate_vfe() calls calculate_kl_divergence() with the same arguments and immediately echoes the result
The function adds no logic — VFE and KL divergence are treated as identical, which may be intentionally simplified but the wrapper adds indirection without behavior
issues.suggestion: Either remove calculate_vfe() and call calculate_kl_divergence() directly at the call site, or add the actual VFE computation that distinguishes it from KL divergence (accuracy + complexity terms)

root_causes: set -e used at top of shell scripts but then redundant $? checks added below — inconsistent application of error handling strategy creates dead code throughout
Shell scripting limitation: loop variable 'action' is syntactically valid but not passed to called functions — the code compiles/runs silently while the logic is broken
likely_symptoms: Active inference simulation always selects actions in a non-EFE-dependent way (first or last environment state wins)
Success celebration message '🎉 All implementations completed' never displays when running a specific language
possible_false_positives: status_dashboard.sh show_recent_activity() -printf flag — this is a portability issue rather than a logic issue; the logic is correct for Linux systems
